summary: Scheduled sweeps complement change-local gates by detecting accumulated, external and cross-cutting risk, provided results are comparable, owned and connected to remediation.

points.text: Dependency-network research shows that exposure can change without a repository commit, so event-only checks cannot cover newly disclosed vulnerabilities or newly available fixes.
Whole-system sweeps can find erosion, orphaned ownership, stale documentation and policy drift that no single pull request crosses visibly.
Using the same verdict, evidence, severity and waiver schema as per-change gates enables trend comparison and avoids a second remediation workflow.
A sweep without an owner, service-level target and deduplication merely produces a recurring backlog; completion means triage and closure, not successful execution.
